name: metric-card

frames.best_why: Frame 1 is fully at rest: total, full trend line and all three breakdown rows.

tagline: A revenue tile whose figure rolls and chart re-shades as you scrub the days.
summary: A card showing a metric total, its change against the previous period, a shaded trend line and a three-part breakdown. Dragging across the chart selects a day or a range and the number and captions update.
appearance: A tall dark rounded card: a Revenue label with 7D, 30D and 90D pills at the top, a huge white figure below with a small green or red percentage, then a white area chart over a dashed prior line, orange event ticks and three weighted bars with labelled value rows.
behaviour: Hovering or dragging on the chart reads a single day or a span, rolling the figure and lighting only that slice while the caption names the compared dates; a dragged range stays until Clear is pressed. The period pills morph the line into a new shape.
demo_content: A Revenue card with Plans, Usage and Services segments, a $51,612 total and events Fall promo and New pricing.
search_phrases: kpi card with sparkline and total
drag across chart to pick dates
number that counts as you hover
use_when: A dashboard needs one headline number that can also be examined day by day or over a dragged range.
avoid_when: It needs at least twice the longest period of daily data, or the previous-period comparison line goes flat.
customise: Pass label, segment names, daily data, event notes, periods, default period and currency through props; the colour palette and chart geometry are constants in the source.
weight_why: An SVG path morph on a requestAnimationFrame loop plus rolling digit transitions.

a11y.note: Coverage is strong; the one gap is that selecting a range needs Shift plus arrow keys on the chart slider.

issues: In frames 2 to 4 the big figure is caught mid-roll, so its digits look garbled or doubled.
The dashed comparison line and orange event ticks are faint against the dark chart.
polish_why: Rich micro-chart with strong hierarchy; mid-roll digits and faint reference lines blur it.
